QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_31

question.text: For domestic-violence resolution under SAS-400, the MOST suitable OUTCOME indicator to audit is:

answer.text: Number of helpline calls received (this is demand / activity)
Number of DV cases legally resolved / referred to One-Stop Centres + victim's self-reported safety-perception score 6 months post-intervention

explanation.text: The Logic: Domestic-violence resolution is inherently multi-dimensional. A defensible OUTCOME indicator captures both an objective resolution dimension (cases legally resolved or referred to established support mechanisms such as One-Stop Centres) and a subjective dimension (the victim's own safety-perception, measured a few months post-intervention to test sustainability). Outputs and activity counts alone do not evidence outcome. The Trap: Options A and C are activity/output counts — they say nothing about whether the situation was resolved. Option D is publicity material, not impact evidence. Note: The cited SIA workbook pages do not discuss domestic-violence resolution, One-Stop Centres, legal case resolution, or a six-month victim safety-perception score under SAS-400. The framing above reflects general outcome-measurement practice for gender-equity programmes rather than a workbook-page citation.
